problems.title: A graph meeting every straight line
problems.question: How many of x³,ax²,tan x,e³ˣ,log₃(x+2),1/x have a graph intersecting every line in the plane?
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: For x³, every nonvertical line gives an odd cubic equation; every vertical line has a valid graph point.
steps: x³−mx−b has opposite infinite limits and hence a real zero, so y=x³ intersects every nonvertical line as well.
Each other function fails: ax² misses some horizontal lines; tan x misses vertical pole lines; the exponential misses y=0; the logarithm misses vertical lines outside its domain; 1/x misses x=0.
Only one graph qualifies.

problems.title: A tangent parallel to a given line
problems.question: f(x)=x²−3x+2. Find the tangent-point abscissa for a tangent parallel to 2x+y=5.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: The given slope is −2; f′(x)=2x−3.

problems.title: Sum of focal distances on an ellipse
problems.question: A=(√7,12√2/5). Find the sum of its distances to the foci of x²/25+y²/16=1.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: An ellipse point has sum of focal distances 2a.
steps: Check A lies on the ellipse: 7/25+(288/25)/16=7/25+18/25=1.
The semimajor axis is 5, so the focal-distance sum is 10.

problems.title: Surface area of a sphere inscribed in a cone
problems.question: A cone has slant height 5 and base radius 3. Find its insphere surface area.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: h=√(l²−R²); sphere radius r=Rh/(R+l); surface=4πr².
steps: h=4 and r=3×4/(3+5)=3/2. Thus surface=4π×9/4=9π.

problems.title: A common tangent plane and the line of centres
problems.question: Spheres have radii 2,3 and centre distance 7. A common tangent plane meets their centre line at A. Which listed AO₁ is possible?
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: The right triangles to a common tangent plane give AO₁:AO₂=2:3.
steps: For a tangent plane leaving both centres on one side, A lies outside the centre segment and AO₂−AO₁=7. The ratio gives AO₁=14.
For a separating tangent plane, AO₁+AO₂=7 and AO₁=14/5. Only 14 is listed.

problems.title: Slant asymptote of a rational function
problems.question: Find the slant asymptote of (2x²+3x−1)/(x−3).
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Polynomial division: f(x)=2x+9+26/(x−3).
steps: The last term tends to zero at infinity. The slant asymptote is y=2x+9.

problems.title: Cancellation in inverse-trigonometric derivatives
problems.question: Evaluate (arcsin x)′√(1−x²)−(arccos x)′√(1−x²).
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Derivatives are 1/√(1−x²) and −1/√(1−x²), for |x|<1.
steps: The two products are 1 and −1. Their difference is 2.

problems.title: A cosine square with a cubic inner function
problems.question: f(x)=cos²(x³). Find f′(1).
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Chain rule gives f′(x)=−6x²cos(x³)sin(x³)=−3x²sin(2x³).
steps: At x=1 the value is −3sin2, with 2 measured in radians.

problems.title: A cylinder and its insphere have matching areas
problems.question: A sphere is inscribed in a cylinder whose lateral area is 64. Find the sphere surface area.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: The cylinder has radius r and height 2r; lateral area=2πr(2r)=4πr².
steps: The last expression is exactly the sphere surface area, so it too equals 64.

problems.title: Focal distances at a hyperbola vertex
problems.question: On x²/9−y²/16=1 a point has x=3. Which listed distance to a focus is possible?
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
steps: The foci are (±5,0). The two distances are 2 and 8; only 8 is listed.
problems.answer: 8 among the choices; the two distances are 2 and 8.

problems.title: Area of a logarithm’s two-dimensional domain
problems.question: Find the area of all (x,y) where log base (3−|y|) of (2−|x|) is defined.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Argument>0; base>0 and base≠1.
steps: Require |x|<2, |y|<3 and |y|≠2. The region is the open 4-by-6 rectangle with two horizontal lines removed.
Those lines have zero area, so the area remains 24.

problems.title: Nearest point on a line to the origin
problems.question: Find the point on 4x+3y+25=0 nearest the origin.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: The closest point is the perpendicular foot, a scalar multiple of normal (4,3).
steps: Write the point as t(4,3). Then 25t+25=0 gives t=−1, so the point is (−4,−3).

problems.title: Reciprocal logarithms require a first-quadrant domain
problems.question: Solve log base sin x of cos x =2−log base cos x of sin x.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Both sine and cosine must be positive and not 1. Put t=logₛᵢₙₓ(cos x); the other logarithm is 1/t.
steps: t+1/t=2 gives t=1, hence sin x=cos x. Positivity of both restricts x to the first quadrant modulo 2π.
Thus x=π/4+2kπ; solutions in other quadrants are excluded by the logarithm bases and arguments.

problems.title: A horizontal plane through a point
problems.question: Find the plane perpendicular to the z axis through (1,−2,3).
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Its normal is parallel to (0,0,1).
steps: The plane therefore has constant z, equal to the point’s coordinate 3.

problems.title: Two parallel-section area ratios in a tetrahedron
problems.question: Tetrahedron ABCD has S(ABC)=4S(ABD). M on CD has CM:MD=2:1. Through M take sections parallel to ABC and ABD. Find their area ratio in that order.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Parallel sections scale areas by the square of their vertex-to-section edge fraction.
steps: The section parallel to ABC is viewed from D, with DM/DC=1/3, so its area is S(ABC)/9.
The section parallel to ABD is viewed from C, with CM/CD=2/3, so its area is 4S(ABD)/9.
These are equal because S(ABC)=4S(ABD).

problems.title: Distinct roots must not be counted with multiplicity
problems.question: For which listed a is the sum of squares of distinct real roots of x³−2ax²+(2a²−6a+8)x=0 greatest?
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Factor out x. The quadratic discriminant is 4[1−(a−3)²].
steps: At listed a=0,1,−1 the quadratic has no real roots, leaving only zero. At a=2 it has repeated root 2, so the distinct-root squared sum is 4.
At a=4 the repeated root is 4, giving sum 16. At a=3 the nonzero roots are 2 and 4, giving sum 4+16=20.
The maximum among the listed cases is at a=3.

problems.title: Minimum of a quartic on an interval
problems.question: Find the minimum of 4x⁴−2x²−5 on [0,2].
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
steps: The square vanishes at x=1/2, which is in the interval. The minimum is −21/4.

problems.title: A zero radical factor adds a root
problems.question: Find the sum of solutions of (x−10)(x−4)√(log₃x−2)=0.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: The domain is x≥9.
steps: x=10 is valid; x=4 is outside the domain. The radical vanishes at log₃x=2, giving x=9.
The root sum is 10+9=19.

problems.title: A plane containing a line and a parallel direction
problems.question: Find the plane through M=(3,−2,1),N=(2,4,3), parallel to (2,1,3).
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: A normal is MN×n, with MN=(−1,6,2).
steps: The cross product is (16,7,−13). The plane is 16(x−3)+7(y+2)−13(z−1)=0.
Simplify to 16x+7y−13z−21=0.

problems.title: Distance from a base vertex to a spatial diagonal line
problems.question: A cylinder’s base contains right triangle ABC with hypotenuse AC=2√6 and AB=√6. CC₁=2√3. Find distance from B to line AC₁.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: Point-to-line distance squared=|AB|²−(AB·AC₁)²/|AC₁|².
steps: Choose A=(0,0,0),C=(2√6,0,0),B=(√6/2,3/√2,0),C₁=(2√6,0,2√3). These satisfy the right-triangle lengths.
|AB|²=6, |AC₁|²=36 and AB·AC₁=6. Distance squared=6−36/36=5.

problems.title: An increasing cubic for every real input
problems.question: Find all a for which f(x)=2x³−3(a+2)x²+48ax+6x−3 is increasing on R.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: f′=6[x²−(a+2)x+8a+1]. An upward quadratic is nonnegative everywhere iff its discriminant is nonpositive.
steps: The discriminant is (a+2)²−4(8a+1)=a²−28a=a(a−28).
Require a(a−28)≤0, giving 0≤a≤28. Isolated derivative zeros at the endpoints do not prevent strict increase.

problems.title: Increasing through an absolute-value corner
problems.question: Find the increasing interval of f(x)=6x³−3|x−1|.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: For x<1, f′=18x²+3; for x>1, f′=18x²−3.
steps: The first derivative is always positive; the second is positive because x>1. The function is continuous at 1.
Thus it increases on the whole real line, including across its corner.

problems.title: Minimize the maximum among listed parameters
problems.question: For which listed a is the maximum on [0,2] of x³/3−(a+3)x²/2+3ax smallest?
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: The coefficient of a is 3x−x²/2≥0 on [0,2].
steps: The listed a=−3 makes f(x)=x³/3−9x≤0 throughout [0,2], with maximum 0 at x=0.
Every other listed a is positive, making f(x)>0 for sufficiently small positive x; its maximum is therefore greater than zero.
So a=−3 gives the least maximum.

problems.title: Volume of the maximum-lateral-area cylinder in a sphere
problems.question: Find the volume of a cylinder inscribed in a radius-R sphere when its lateral area is maximal.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: r²+h²/4=R² and lateral area=2πrh.
steps: Maximizing rh=2r√(R²−r²) is equivalent to maximizing r²(R²−r²), achieved at r²=R²/2.
Then h=√2R. Volume=πr²h=πR³/√2.

problems.title: A plane normal to a given line through a divided segment
problems.question: A=(3,5,0),B=(−2,1,3),C=(2,4,−6),D=(5,7,12). K divides CK:KD=1:2. Find the plane through K perpendicular to AB.
problems.idea: Use exact differentiation or geometry, then verify endpoints, domains and exceptional cases.
formulas: K=(2C+D)/3; a normal to the plane is AB.
steps: K=(3,5,0), coincidentally A. AB=(−5,−4,3).
The plane is −5(x−3)−4(y−5)+3z=0, equivalent to 5x+4y−3z−35=0.
